summary: Frontend-only E2E testing of redesigned Payment (SO) page + Security Officer Social Security Code. Logged in as admin@example.com. Verified: client list landing (Arseas Security / ARS / 1 officer / View), navigation via both client-name link and View button, client view header + Add New Payment + search + PDF/Excel buttons, 9-column records table with correct values (W2 1000, DD 300, Zelle 200, W9 Total 500, Total 1500) and matching grand-total footer, officer searchable dropdown (by name 'john', officer code ARS297002, email, phone - all returned 1 option), full Add New Payment submit with upsert behaviour (row count stayed 1, values updated to 1200/400/100 -> total 1700), Edit flow (officer fixed, all 3 rows pre-filled with date/txn/amount, changing Zelle 100->250 recomputed W9 Total 650 and Total/Grand Total 1850), search filter (no match => 0 rows, 'SSC-123' => 1 row), PDF and Excel downloads both fired real downloads (Payment-Arseas Security.pdf / .xlsx), persistence verified after full page reload, and multi-officer flow (created TEST_QA officer with SSC + email, new record created as separate row, grand totals summed correctly across 2 rows, then record + officer deleted). Officers list shows Social Security Code column and Add form has field-social_security_code which saves and displays correctly. No console errors (other than expected 401 from /auth/me pre-login). All tested flows passed; no blocking issues found.

issues: Records table header uses a pink (#F2C4CE) band that is stylistically inconsistent with the neutral #F8FAFC headers used on every other dispatch table (client list, officers list) - intentional? worth confirming with design
Officer search dropdown has no keyboard navigation (arrow keys/Enter) and no clear/X to reset a selected officer; user must delete the text to re-search

critical_code_review_comments: OfficerSearch does not search by Social Security Code (SSC-QA-777 returned 0 options) even though the dropdown displays SSC. Spec only requires Name/Code/Email/Phone so this is informational, but adding SSC to the backend search fields would be consistent.

PaymentSOPage.js: client-view navigation is pure React state, so a browser refresh drops the user back to the client list. Consider a URL param (?client_id=) for deep-linkable/back-button-friendly navigation.
download() catch shows a generic '<KIND> download failed' toast and swallows the server detail; surface formatApiErrorDetail for easier debugging.
